notes: Too little data + too high LR; model barely moved from baseline.
Healthy loss behavior (not overfit) but WER still regressed -- read as undertraining.
First run to beat baseline. Two variables changed at once vs v3 (full fine-tune + more epochs) -- doesn't isolate which mattered. ~13min on Colab GPU vs v3's ~6.5hr on MPS.

Not a training run -- a manifest cleanup pass: re-queried LRCLIB for every billboard-sourced record's claimed duration and compared it against the actual downloaded audio's duration, dropping 37/81 songs where they diverged by more than 5s (almost certainly the wrong YouTube edit matched to that song's lyrics). Also filtered near-empty/symbol-only lyrics segments (e.g. a lone '♪' for an instrumental break) before chunking, and added small padding at chunk boundaries since LRCLIB line timestamps are approximate.

Same method/epochs/lr as v4 -- only changed variable is data quality (see data-fixup-1): dropped 37/81 duration-mismatched songs, filtered near-empty segments, added chunk-boundary padding. Isolates whether the v4 win was really about full-finetune+epochs, or was partly capped/helped by the data bugs fixed here.

Phase 2 ablation: same clean data + 5 epochs as v5, but LoRA instead of full fine-tune -- isolates whether v4/v5's win came from full fine-tuning or just from epochs/clean data. Compare this WER against v5's 55.1% to tell which.

Phase 3: fewer epochs (2 vs v5's 5) of full fine-tune, same clean data, to fix v5's overfitting (train_loss 0.03, eval_loss flat ~1.2-1.3). Result: the train/eval loss gap is genuinely healthier (0.15 vs 1.08, vs v5's 0.03 vs 1.28) but WER is worse (63.1% vs v5's 55.1%, barely better than the 66.2% baseline). So overfitting isn't simply costing WER here -- v5's extra epochs bought real accuracy even while memorizing the train split; cutting epochs lost more than it fixed. v5 remains the best result so far. Next lever to try: more data (the in-progress 200-song build) rather than fewer epochs, so the model has enough train diversity to keep training longer without just memorizing.

First run on the expanded 119-song deduped dataset (up from 34 cleaned songs for v5/LoRA-ablation/v6-short) -- more training diversity is the lever being tested here, not epochs or method. Training crashed once before this (Taylor Swift 'Babylon' produced a 509-token label chunk against Whisper's 448-token cap); fixed by dropping over-cap chunks in _build_hf_dataset. This run completed training cleanly but the SSH session dropped during/after eval, so this eval was re-run standalone against the saved checkpoint.

Scales both levers past v7: much larger dataset (v3 manifest, 248 songs pulled from 100 weeks of Billboard history vs. v7's 102-song/20-week set) and more epochs (8 vs. v7's 5), testing whether a bigger/more diverse training set tolerates more training before memorizing. Result: worse than v7 (54.6% vs. 52.4% WER), and train/eval loss confirms why -- train_loss collapsed to ~0.003 (near-total memorization) while eval_loss rose to 1.73, the worst of any full-finetune run so far (vs. v7's 1.32, v5's 1.28). So 8 epochs overfit on 190 songs; more data did NOT buy tolerance for more epochs the way the v6-short writeup speculated -- that conclusion doesn't generalize to larger datasets. v7's 5 epochs remains the best epoch/data-size balance found so far. This run's SSH session dropped at step 668/1336 (end of epoch 4/8) because colab_run.sh launched training in the foreground at the time; resumed from the epoch-4 checkpoint for epochs 5-8 rather than restarting. colab_run.sh now launches training detached (nohup) so this shouldn't recur.
